summary: Orbiting The Earth is an interactive 3D observatory that helps users investigate how Earth’s environment is changing. Choose a location and an environmental variable, explore decades of NASA data, and see how much the variable has changed and whether the trend is statistically significant. Users can compare locations, explore regional differences on 3D maps, and examine how observed trends could extend into the future. The project brings geographic exploration, time-series visualization, and statistical analysis into one workflow for students and the public.
details:
Orbiting The Earth helps students and the public investigate environmental change through an interactive 3D globe. Users choose a location and a variable such as temperature, precipitation, or soil moisture. The application retrieves historical data from NASA POWER, visualizes the time series, estimates the rate of change per decade, and presents confidence intervals and Mann–Kendall test results so users can assess the evidence.

The globe connects each investigation to a real place. Users can filter recent natural events, open a climate case file, compare two locations, and explore differences across a country’s divisions in 3D. The projection slider shows how environmental variables could change if observed trends continue. The application explains the assumptions and uncertainty behind those estimates.

We built the frontend with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Three.js, and the backend with Python, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL/PostGIS. We designed the interface for desktop and touch devices and prioritized clear source attribution, readable explanations, and explicit handling of missing data.

Our approach brings the four steps of the challenge into one experience: choose a variable, select a region, visualize its historical record, and assess the trend. This helps users answer four questions: What is changing, where, by how much, and how strong is the evidence?

NASA FIRMS — VIIRS active fire detections and multi-year fire archive
NASA Blue Marble — Daytime Earth imagery with shaded relief and bathymetry
NASA Black Marble — VIIRS nighttime Earth imagery
NASA Terra MODIS MOD13A1 Version 6.1 — Vegetation Index (NDVI) for regional vegetation analysis
projectRefs: USGS Earthquake Catalog — Earthquake locations, magnitudes, and depths
NOAA IBTrACS — Historical tropical cyclone tracks
NOAA Storm Prediction Center — Tornado reports
NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center — OVATION aurora model
Open-Meteo — Weather and air quality data
PB2002 — Global tectonic plate boundaries by Peter Bird
